summary: Go's pmdoc Parse gives an email autolink (ast.AutoLinkEmail: a GFM literal a@b.test or a CommonMark <a@b.test>) the href 'mailto:' + address, as remark-gfm does. Render is unchanged: such a link is stored as [addr](mailto:addr), which main already writes for explicit mailto links and which Go and the browser engine read back alike, so no stored markdown changes bytes. Tests are written first and run red at main + tests: Go rows comparing Go to the engine, byte-stability rows, and a Playwright test asserting the stored markdown, the live-editor and past-version hrefs and what the editor's link opener passes to window.open.

tasks.title: The fix
tasks.detail: case *ast.AutoLink (:957-958): href := string(current.URL(source)); if current.AutoLinkType == ast.AutoLinkEmail { href = "mailto:" + href }; use href in the link mark. Do not change Render, linkify.go, literalURL or literalLength (the renderer reads literalLength, render.go:707,731).

decisionsForArchitect.decision: Scope of the email-boundary divergences left after this fix
decisionsForArchitect.detail: Seven shapes still read differently in Go and the editor: an email after punctuation (x;a@b.test, mailto:a@b.test, xmpp:a@b.test), www.a@b.test, a local part holding ' or !, a domain ending in a digit (a@b.test1). Fixing them needs Go to read email literals as micromark does, including after punctuation where goldmark asks no inline parser (linkify.go:40-49) — the mechanism INFRA-531 must build for web addresses in the same linkify.go.
decisionsForArchitect.recommendation: Add them to INFRA-531's scope; this plan records them as agree:false rows in email_readback_test.go for INFRA-531 to flip.

decisionsForArchitect.detail: The fix does not touch an explicit link (parse.go:947-955) and live trees load from Yjs history, so existing documents such as dispatch://INFRA/artifact/goals-md keep the bare target.
decisionsForArchitect.recommendation: No bulk rewrite: each rewrite mints a version, and on an approved spec closes its design gate. goals-md's owner fixes its one link with dispatch doc-edit after the deploy.
